answer: Because the violet calculation reruns each epoch, the ripple weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the vine settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 104 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 54% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 21 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
